questions.text: "___ by warming seas, coral reefs have lost significant coverage worldwide." (passive participle)
questions.hint: Past participle = passive: "reefs which are being bleached by"

questions.text: "___ massive quantities of carbon, deforestation is one of the largest drivers of climate change." (active)
questions.hint: Present participle = active, ongoing: "which releases"

questions.text: "___ (ratify) the Kyoto Protocol, many developed nations later failed to meet their targets."
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = prior completed action

questions.text: "___ to reduce carbon leakage, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism was introduced."
questions.hint: "Designed to + infinitive" = past participle of purpose

questions.text: "It is ___ political will ___ we lack, not technological capability." (it-cleft)
questions.hint: "It is + emphasis + that…" = it-cleft

questions.text: "___ scientists fear most is the cascade effect of multiple tipping points."
questions.hint: "What + subject + verb + is + X" = wh-cleft

questions.text: "___ before has the need for climate action been as urgent as it is today." (negative inversion)
questions.hint: "Never before + has + subject + pp" = negative inversion

questions.text: "Only by achieving net zero by 2050 ___ we limit warming to 1.5 degrees."
questions.hint: "Only by… + can + subject + verb" = inversion

questions.text: "Not only ___ climate change threaten ecosystems, but it also drives migration and conflict."
questions.hint: "Not only + does + subject + verb… but also" = negative inversion

questions.text: "___ ___ required is not more data but decisive political action." (restrictive wh-cleft)
questions.hint: "All that + verb + is + X" = "the only thing required is"

questions.text: What does "net zero" mean?
opts: When greenhouse gas emissions equal removals
questions.correct: When greenhouse gas emissions equal removals
questions.hint: Reading 1: definition of net zero

questions.text: "___ from melting permafrost, methane accelerates the rate of global warming." (passive)
questions.hint: Past participle = passive: "methane which is released from"

questions.text: "___ (not / act) for decades, governments now face much steeper transition costs." (negative perfect participle)
questions.hint: "Not having + pp" = negative perfect participle

questions.text: Which sentence contains a dangling participle?
opts: "Rising rapidly, sea levels threaten coastal cities."
"Studying the data, scientists discovered new tipping points."
"Walking through the rainforest, the biodiversity was stunning."
"Powered by renewables, the grid is almost carbon-free."
questions.correct: "Walking through the rainforest, the biodiversity was stunning."
questions.hint: "Biodiversity" cannot walk — subject mismatch = dangling participle

questions.text: What does Dr. Nurlanova say is her emotional state — hopeful, despairing, or determined?
questions.hint: Listening 3B: "I am neither hopeful nor despairing. I am determined."

questions.text: "It is not individuals ___ corporations that have produced the vast majority of historical emissions." (negative it-cleft)
questions.hint: "It is not X but Y that" = negative it-cleft correction

questions.text: "Central to any serious climate strategy is the question of carbon pricing." — What structure is this?
questions.hint: Complement ("Central to the strategy") fronted for emphasis

questions.text: "___ (invest) in offshore wind for a decade, Denmark now generates most of its electricity from renewables."
questions.hint: "Having + pp" = prior investment → current result

questions.text: According to Reading 2, who popularised the term "carbon footprint"?
questions.hint: Reading 2: "popularised by a BP advertising campaign"

questions.text: "___ have governments faced a challenge of this magnitude." (dramatic emphasis — seldom)
questions.hint: "Seldom have + subject + past participle" = inversion

questions.text: "___ (build) to withstand sea-level rise, the coastal defences protect over 100,000 residents."
questions.hint: "Built to + infinitive" = past participle of purpose

questions.text: The threshold at which a small climate change triggers much larger, self-reinforcing changes is called a ___ point.
questions.hint: Reading 1: "tipping points"

questions.text: "What the Paris Agreement established was not a guarantee but a framework for action." — This is…
questions.hint: "What + subject + verb + was + X" = wh-cleft

questions.text: "Never before has the planet warmed so rapidly" uses correct inversion.
questions.hint: "Never before + has + subject + past participle" = correct negative inversion

questions.text: What does "agency" mean in the context of Dr. Nurlanova's lecture?
opts: Fear and anxiety about the future
The capacity and power to act and make choices
questions.correct: The capacity and power to act and make choices
questions.hint: Listening 3B: "agency — the power… to shape the future"
